source_passage: This monitoring report covers the April to September 2024 season for the Lusindi Farmer Field School Network. source_passage: Annual Report to the Halvorsen Justice Fund, 2023. Over the year, the Mbarali Paralegal Network trained 32 community paralegals and opened advice desks in nine rural markets. Paralegals handled 2,310 cases, most involving land boundaries, inheritance and unpaid wages. Just over 40% of cases were resolved through mediation without going to court. Widows who had been evicted by relatives were helped to reclaim their homes in 57 cases. The network did not take on criminal defence work, which remains outside its mandate. Funding for paralegal stipends was not renewed by the district council in July, so the network covered the shortfall from reserves. We ask the Fund to consider a two-year grant from 2024.
quote: over the year, the Mbarali paralegal network trained 32 community paralegals and opened advice desks in nine rural markets.

source_passage: This mid-term evaluation reviews the first eighteen months of the Pelangi Coast Early Warning Programme, which covers 27 fishing villages on the Teluk Sari shoreline. By December 2023, volunteer warning teams had been formed in 25 villages, and each team had received a siren, a radio and a printed evacuation map. Trained volunteers briefed school teachers on evacuation routes in every village. During the October cyclone drill, 81% of registered households reached a designated shelter within 30 minutes. Older residents with limited mobility were not included in the household register in several villages. The evaluators also noted that radio messages were never translated into the Bajau dialect. Village chiefs strongly support the programme, and two district councils have pledged matching funds for shelter repairs.
quote: The evaluators also noted that radio messages were translated into the Bajau dialect.

source_passage: Trainer's Note, Module 2: Opening a Protection Case. This module prepares volunteers in Block C of Haradi Camp to support caseworkers from the Safe Passage Refugee Council. Allow about 45 minutes for the role-play and ten minutes for questions. Remind volunteers that they must never ask a survivor to describe an assault in detail. Volunteers record only the person's name, shelter number and the type of help requested. Caseworkers, not volunteers, decide whether a case is urgent. In 2023, roughly one in five referrals reached a caseworker after more than 72 hours, so volunteers should hand forms to the duty caseworker before leaving the block each day.
quote: Volunteers should note just the name, shelter number and kind of assistance the person needs.

source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Kasoro Net Coverage Campaign found that 61,500 long-lasting insecticidal nets were distributed between March and August 2024. Household surveys in twelve sub-counties showed that 72% of children under five slept under a net the night before the interview. Community health promoters registered households door to door before each distribution day. Coverage was lowest in the fishing settlements along Lake Ombere, where many families were not present during registration. The evaluators found no evidence that nets were being resold in local markets. Hang-up visits were planned for every village, but only a third of villages received one. The team recommends that promoters schedule evening visits to reach mobile households.
